headline: Lahaina Rebuild Design Review

meeting.summary: The board approved a new home at 1191 Front Street and deferred review of a Lahaina fire rebuild at 1429 Front Street.
meeting.recap: The Urban Design Review Board meeting was called to order at 10:02.[[0:00:30]] Staff said the first project needs board review because it sits in the special management area, a coastal zone.[[0:02:16]] The first item was a new single-family home at 1191 Front Street.[[0:03:02]] A board member asked for a more detailed list of exterior colors and materials.[[0:29:57]] The board voted to approve the first project.[[0:43:39]] The second project also asks for a shoreline setback variance, which is permission to build closer to the ocean than rules allow.[[0:44:47]] The owner plans to raise the home above flood level plus 3.2 feet for sea level rise and one foot more.[[0:49:00]] A board member said the drawings show the 40-foot shoreline setback line landing in the middle of the main house.[[1:23:23]] The chair said one plan sheet shows the home at 10.2 feet above sea level, but the owner described 14.2 feet.[[1:56:48]] The board voted to defer, or postpone, its review until more accurate drawings are ready.[[2:01:51]] The next meeting is Wednesday, November 4, because Tuesday is election day.[[2:03:24]]
meeting.next: Staff said the board's design recommendations on the second item go to the Maui Planning Commission, which will take public testimony at a future date. The owner said he will make sure the drawings are redone. Staff said no items are officially on the next agenda yet, but one or two may be scheduled.
